reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence - peripheral OX40 receptor occupancy >80% achieved in combination arms, with measurable soluble OX40 levels and receptor occupancy on CD4+ T cells and Tregs. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Evidence of biological activity - sustained T cell expansion was assessed, suggesting downstream immune activation occurred. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Mixed results - 8 responses observed but only in combination arms, with 0 responses in monotherapy. 24-week PFS rates varied widely (0-42.9%). 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Clear subgroup effect - efficacy only seen with combination therapy (BMS-986178 + nivolumab ± ipilimumab), suggesting OX40 agonism requires concurrent checkpoint inhibition. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a dose escalation/safety study, not powered for efficacy. High toxicity burden may have limited optimal dosing.
